statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6467 (PostgreSQL extension script schema mishandling executes arbitrary SQL) in 17.12 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6467/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17 (versions before 17.12 are affected), and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, list this CVE. The fix is two commits on the REL_17_STABLE branch: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/79f9793fc44c75d3096ef67677a729ad21a89c2c, which uses locking to block the ALTER SCHEMA ... RENAME attack on CREATE EXTENSION and ALTER EXTENSION, and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5c751533737eb08c97d6816e43039324e34bad42, which makes them reject a temporary schema or the '$user' placeholder as the extension schema. Together they change src/backend/commands/extension.c, src/backend/commands/schemacmds.c and src/backend/catalog/namespace.c; both are tagged Security: CVE-2026-6467 and are in the REL_17_12 release tag and not in REL_17_11. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6467. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in the postgresql17 package. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies, in this or the earlier revisions the published builds came from, touch the source files this fix changes, and Alpine lists CVE-2026-6467 under its 17.12-r0 secfixes. We checked every postgresql17 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-28 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), both the postgresql17 and postgresql17-client packages, on x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: the server binary of each build reports the PostgreSQL release of the same version (17.7, 17.8, 17.9, 17.10, 17.11 and 17.12). Of these, 17.12-r0 carry the fix, and 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0 are affected. As a check, the server binary in 17.12-r0 contains the error message the second commit adds, 'unacceptable extension schema name "%s"', and the server binary in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0 does not, on both architectures. 17.12-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6467, an uncontrolled search path element in CREATE EXTENSION and ALTER EXTENSION that lets an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege make a trusted-extension script run arbitrary SQL as the bootstrap superuser, via ALTER SCHEMA ... RENAME or CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA "$user", in 17.12. Within major version 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6467/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6467. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
